fixes.explanation: Yes. The passage says, “Hammered silver is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz…” So the passage names where the metals come from. That's a whole shipping order for something that can't walk to the door.

That's right. The passage says the idols' clothes are blue and purple, “…all fashioned by skilled workers.” So the outfit comes from people who know their craft. And the idol can't even hold still without nails.

Priests aren't mentioned in these verses. The passage says their clothes are blue and purple, “…all fashioned by skilled workers.” The ones who fashioned them are skilled workers. I think that's a lot of effort for something that won't thank them.

Lions would make a great roar, but they aren't in this verse. The passage says, “When He thunders, the waters in the heavens roar…” The roaring in this verse comes from the waters in the heavens. Lions never get a mention.
Hold on, friend, it says the opposite. The passage says, “every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols.” Shame, not pride. The goldsmith's own idols are what put him to shame.

Blessing is a nice word, but it isn't what the text says. It says the molten images are a fraud, and there is no breath in them. A fraud and a blessing are two very different things, friend. The verse says these images have no breath at all.
This one's actually in the passage, friend. It says, “…Israel is the tribe of His inheritance…” So the statement is true. After all those idols, the passage ends by naming Israel as His inheritance.
